   INTERVENOR GEORGE NOELKE’S NOTICE OF LEGISLATIVE TESTIMONY

COMES NOW, George Noelke (“Noelke”), pro se Intervenor in CCN 59182 and 59475 appearing
conditionally and solely to provide notice of his public testimony at the House State Affairs Committee
hearing on August 19, 2026.​
His testimony at Attachment A has been filed with the Committee online on August 18, 2026.​
His filing of this notice in 59182 is not a waiver of his earlier arguments that both SOAH and the PUC
have lost subject matter jurisdiction in this matter. The 180 day rule in PURA § 37.057 (missed by
the PUC in 59182) has been ruled by SOAH (at Item 581 in 59182) as mandatory but not



                                                                                                          1
 jurisdictional. Noelke has argued to the contrary that it is jurisdictional and therefore subject
matter jurisdiction has been lost. The Applicants agree with Noelke as the administrative record
already shows that they have cited legislative history for the proposition that the 180 day rule is
jurisdictional. The inconsistent interpretation of the law by SOAH (that has the effect of
unlawfully enlarging their jurisdiction) makes 59182 ideal for review under § 2001.174 of the
Texas APA should the PUC nonetheless award the CCN to Applicants.​
Noelke is not seeking any relief relating to this notice. He further acknowledges that his legislative
testimony is not evidence in either 59182 or 59475.​
​
Dated: August 19, 2026

Respectfully submitted,​
​
​
/s/ George Noelke​
George Noelke​
Intervenor​
Pro se Landowner

                                         Attachment A


                          Written Testimony of George Noelke​
                         House State Affairs Committee Hearing
                         Regarding 765 kV Transmission Lines​
                                    August 19, 2026

My name is George Noelke, and I am a landowner in Irion County. I am also an intervenor in
CCN 59182 and 59475. I also testified in the Senate Business and Commerce hearing. See Item
6426 in 59475.

I would like to address the Applicants Joint TSPSs’ Response to ASL’s Motion to Abate filed on
August 18, the day before this hearing.

Notwithstanding my arguments in multiple filings in 59475, the Applicants have the audacity to
assert in their filing: “If there were a due process issue, the remedy is not abatement…[T]he
remedy for a denial of due process is due process.” Univ. of Tex. Med. Sch. v. Than, 901 S.W.
2d 926, 933 (Tex. 1995).​

If Applicants think that “the remedy for a denial of due process is due process” then they
need to personally notice that to the 839 Intervenors they had dismissed in 59475.​

I raised the very case cited by Applicants, the seminal Texas case on procedural due process, and
the Applicants never rebutted my argument. See Item 5105 in 59475. That the Applicants
purport to honor due process after the record is closed is disingenuous and misleading. ​

If the Applicants are such ardent supporters of due process today, then they should have offered
argument during the hearings on the merits. Their ruthless dismissal of more than half the 59475
class of Intervenors transparently shows how they weaponized the 180 day rule to their
advantage, and then remained quiet.​
​
I have recommended that ALL of the 765 kV cases be dismissed by the PUC acting to rescind
their referral to SOAH. SOAH has only the authority given it by the PUC, and once that
authority is withdrawn these cases immediately die. A similar approach, denying the CCN’s, is
the position taken by Chairman Schwertner after the July 29 hearing. An outright dismissal or
rescission of the referral (not an abatement) has the significant advantage of terminating the
ongoing legal expenses of hundreds, if not thousands, of Texas Landowners who have never
asked for a thing in this case but to have their land freed from the unyielding jaws of the


                                                                                                 3
 Applicants who are attempting to take their land without due process.​

A rescission or dismissal would also have the effect of putting the burden back where it should
be: on the Applicants. They chose the strategies to get the case where it is today, dividing it up
into numerous CCN’s as they did. They are the ones who chose to interpret the Permian Basin
Reliability Plan as a blank check for 765 kV transmission lines not connected to generation
plants. Indeed, the Business and Commerce Committee conceded in the July 29 hearing that the
PBRP was intended to only be a legislative study, not the backbone for the justification of the
765 kV lines now proposed.
​
I urge this Committee to recommend to the PUC to rescind their referral to SOAH, outright deny
the applications, or take any other action that will immediately end all of the 765 kV cases before
the legislative session begins.

Thank you for your time.​
George Noelke
